messages:
simon_acme: Hey team, hitting an issue with SSE streaming from Redwood API — final chunk never arrives and JSON is left open. finish_reason is missing. Repro steps below.

jess: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw stream or a minimal curl repro? Which model/region?

simon_acme: model: gpt-redwood-1, region: us-west-2. Using our backend as a proxy -> fastly -> redwood-hosted. Curl I ran: 
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -d '{"input":"long text to force multi-chunk"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Output ends like: 
```
event: message
data: {"id":"tok_abc","delta":"...","finish_reason":
```
and then connection closes. No closing object, no finish_reason value, JSON is cut. Happens ~30% of calls.

jess: thanks — does the client reconnect/resume? any reconnect headers like resume-token?

simon_acme: Our client attempts resume. We see client re-issuing with X-Resume-Offset header, but server returns 200 with partial continuation (no final object). When the client reconnects it sometimes sees leftover trailing bytes "," or an open brace.

jess: pinging eng-sre: @maya @alex — looks like truncated final event on stream with missing finish_reason and dangling JSON. customer reports proxy (Fastly) in path.

maya: can you attach the raw tcp dump or at least the full bytes from the last 2 connections? Also which SDK? Browser or node?

simon_acme: attaching minimal reproduction logs (paste below):
```
--- connection A ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

4
data

500
{"id":"tok_1","choices":[{"delta":"hello","finish_reason":null}]}

0

--- client reconnect ---
GET /v1/stream
X-Resume-Offset: 500

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
chunk: 300
{"id":"tok_1","choices":[{"delta":"world"}]}

<connection closed>
```
Customer says final object with finish_reason never appears.

alex: thanks. two hypotheses: 1) proxy (Fastly) truncates tail on idle/early conn close and strips last SSE event terminator; 2) server sends final event but it gets lost on rejoin/resume handshake because resume logic expects exact byte offsets and small mismatch leaves an unterminated JSON.

maya: also check keepalive/timeouts. If a proxy emits a TCP RST after a linger timeout, client sees abrupt EOF and may not get final chunk. Can you confirm if Fastly is doing any buffering or TLS termination that could interfere?

jess: simon, can you try two quick experiments: 1) hit the regional origin directly (https://us-west-2-origin.redwood.ai/v1/stream) bypassing Fastly to see if the final chunk is present; 2) run curl with --no-buffer and --raw to capture exact bytes, e.g., `curl --no-buffer --raw -v -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" ...` and paste the last 2KB.

simon_acme: will try now. Also noticed deploy-bot rolled out a small runtime patch ~2hrs before incident started. Not sure if related.

deploy-bot: [deploy] runtime/websocket-handler v2026.03.17 rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T15:22:10Z

alex: that deploy touches SSE chunking code. Might be correlated. If direct origin works but Fastly path fails, we have a strong signal for edge buffering/resume mismatch. If origin also fails, it's likely a regression in our runtime.

simon_acme: direct-origin test: final chunk present. Pasting tail: 
```
...{"id":"tok_1","choices":[{"delta":"world","finish_reason":"stop"}]}

[connection closed normally]
```
So origin has correct final object; Fastly path gives cut.

maya: OK that points to edge/proxy. Two short-term mitigations: 1) ask Fastly to increase streaming idle timeout and disable edge buffering for this route; 2) change resume semantics to use event-sequence ids instead of byte offsets so small truncations won't leave an unterminated JSON. We'll open infra ticket to track resume redesign.

alex: I'll prepare a runtime-side guard: when a resume is detected and the first chunk starts with a non-json prefix or leading comma, we can attempt to repair by trimming leading commas and scanning for the first open brace to re-sync. Not ideal but helps clients tolerate tail corruption.

jess: thanks team. Simon — please coordinate with Fastly support (ask them for the exact edge config for streaming and whether they applied any fastly feature flags recently). I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

simon_acme: filed ticket with Fastly and shared trace IDs. Trying their suggested disable of edge-buffering now, will report back in 15m. Thanks!

maya: created infra ticket INF-2026-312 with logs and timeline, tagging runtime and edge teams.

jess: follow-up plan: 1) customer to confirm Fastly change fixed it; 2) eng to ship resume-resilience guard in next runtime patch if needed; 3) product to document known proxy gotchas for customers.

simon_acme: Fastly change fixed it on 3 tests. No truncated tail observed. We'll monitor and report if anything else pops up. Thanks all.

jess: great — closing the loop. Reopen if it reoccurs. :pray:
